content:
The Data Handling chapter is a dependable source of marks in the CTET Paper I (Classes I–V) Mathematics section — and it is one you can master quickly with the right practice. This guide explains what CTET data handling actually tests, the facts and formulas worth memorising, the mistakes that quietly cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now to check where you stand.

Work through the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter-test e-book at the end for full, exam-style practice. That "test → review → practise" loop is how serious CTET candidates turn a weak topic into a strong one.

What Data Handling covers in CTET Paper I Maths

At the primary level this chapter blends content knowledge with pedagogy — how young children learn the idea. Expect questions on:

  • Collecting and organising data
  • Tally marks and tables
  • Pictographs
  • Bar graphs and reading data

Practise the full syllabus free on the CTET Paper I Mathematics course at vidaara.org, then test yourself here.

Key facts and formulas to remember

  • In a tally, a bundle of five is four vertical lines crossed by a fifth.
  • In a pictograph, always read the key — one symbol may stand for more than one item.
  • A bar graph shows values by the height of each bar on a scale.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Ignoring the key of a pictograph and counting symbols as one each.
  • Misreading the scale of a bar graph.

quiz.title: CTET Data Handling Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CTET Paper I – pattern questions on Data Handling. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: A pictograph uses the symbol ☀ to represent 3 sunny days. The row for June has 4 such symbols. How many sunny days were there in June?
A teacher asks students to collect data on the birthdays of their classmates and arrange them month-wise in a table. This activity primarily develops:
questions.explanation: The activity involves gathering real data and organising it systematically, which are fundamental data handling skills.

questions.q: A teacher gives students the following raw data: 'A, B, A, C, A, B, C, A, B'. After constructing a frequency table, what should the sum of the 'Frequency' column be?
questions.explanation: The frequency table will have A: 4, B: 3, C: 2. The sum of the frequency column is the total number of observations listed in the raw data. Total = 4 + 3 + 2 = 9. This sum acts as a check for the table's accuracy.

questions.q: A pictograph uses a heart symbol ♥ to represent 2 students. How many students do 5 such symbols stand for?
A bar graph displays favourite fruits. The scale is: 1 cm on the vertical axis = 2 children. If the bar for Mango is 7.5 cm high, how many children like Mango?
questions.explanation: Number of children = 7.5 cm × 2 children/cm = 15 children.

questions.q: A bar graph shows the number of absentees on different days. The tallest bar indicates:
options: The day with the least absentees
The day with the most absentees
questions.explanation: In a bar graph, the height of a bar represents the value; the tallest bar corresponds to the maximum value, i.e., the day with the most absentees.

questions.q: A pictograph uses the symbol ● to represent 2 apples. Which of the following shows 7 apples correctly?
questions.explanation: 3 full ● give 6 apples, and a half ● gives 1 apple (half of 2). Total = 7 apples.

questions.q: A teacher has data: 45, 90, 75, 30. She wants to create a bar graph with the vertical axis not exceeding 100. Which scale is most suitable for the graph?
questions.explanation: With 1 unit = 10, the highest bar (90) will be 9 units tall, which fits neatly and is easy to draw. Scales like 1 unit = 1 would make bars too tall (up to 90 units), while 1 unit = 2 gives up to 45 units, still large. 1 unit = 5 gives 18 units, manageable but 10 is simpler and more common for such numbers.

questions.q: A pictograph uses the symbol ☺ to represent 2 children. The row for 'Cricket' has 6 such symbols. How many children like Cricket?
questions.explanation: Number of children = Number of symbols × Value of one symbol = 6 × 2 = 12.

questions.q: A pictograph uses the symbol ★ to represent 3 stars. If there are 5 such symbols, how many stars does it represent?

faq.a: A pictograph shows data using pictures or symbols, where each symbol stands for a fixed number given in the key.

faq.q: Why read the key first in a pictograph?
faq.a: Because one symbol often represents more than one item (for example, one face = 2 children), so the count depends on the key.
